subject: Data residency & retention annex — MAP alignment for FinClear evaluation
messages:
From: Remy LaFontaine <remy@finclear.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Data Protection <dataops@finclear.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:15:00 +0000
Subject: Data residency & retention annex — MAP alignment for FinClear evaluation

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week — FinClear's product team is excited about Redwood's latency profile. We're building the MAP and want to lock the security/compliance gating items so our legal and data teams can sign off. Two specific asks from our side: 

1) Residency & data flows: we need confirmation of EU residency (customer data stored in Ireland region) and whether any tokens/derivatives can be replicated to non-EU regions for caching/fallback.

2) Retention & purge SLAs: we prefer a 30-day purge SLA for PII artifacts and 90/365-day windows for logs/usage telemetry. We also need an outbound audit log export format (JSON preferred) and a monthly export cadence.

I've attached our initial DPA annex draft (redlines) and a short matrix. Can you confirm what Redwood can commit to in the MAP (milestones and acceptance criteria)?

Best,
Remy
Product Ops — FinClear

Attachments: DPA_annex_EU_redline.docx (redline)
            retention-matrix.csv (referenced)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Remy LaFontaine <remy@finclear.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Data residency & retention annex — MAP alignment for FinClear evaluation

Remy — thanks for the clear asks and the draft annex. Quick summary of what we can commit to in the MAP and proposed milestones below. Happy to refine language in the DPA annex with legal once we have the milestones agreed.

- Residency: hosted account will be provisioned in eu-west-1 (Ireland). All customer-generated documents, embeddings, and KV caches will be stored in that region by default. Temporary replicas for very short-lived caching within a regionally adjacent fallback are possible but cannot be read by support outside EU without explicit customer consent/opt-in.

- Retention: propose PII artifacts purge window = 30 days after request (implemented via API-driven purge + confirmation). Telemetry & aggregate usage logs: 90 days standard, with option to extend to 365 days under a premium retention add-on (we'll capture this as a MAP checkbox).

- Audit logs: Redwood can provide a monthly export in NDJSON/JSONL format; we can also support on-demand exports for audits. Sample export structure attached (audit-log-sample-20270621.json).

Proposed MAP milestones (dates are placeholders to align with your evaluation runway):
  1) Evidence intake (SIG/CAIQ + SOC2 summary) — 2027-06-28
  2) DPA annex redline agreement — 2027-07-05
  3) Residency & purge verification (test export + purge demo) — 2027-07-12
  4) Final acceptance & procurement sign-off — 2027-07-19

Action items for FinClear: confirm DPA redline comments that require policy change vs. redline language we can accept. On our side Karthik will handle the legal-thread redlines and Laura will coordinate SOC2 artifacts.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: audit-log-sample-20270621.json

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Remy LaFontaine <remy@finclear.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Data residency & retention annex — MAP alignment for FinClear evaluation

Remy / Mina — looping in legal. A few clarifications from our side to avoid late redlines: 

- KMS / key control: we can offer customer-managed keys (BYOK) for EU customers. Key rotation policy is documented and we support HSM-backed keys via AWS KMS — if FinClear requires on-prem HSM we can escalate but that typically adds lead time.

- Data exports & deletion proof: we'll provide an export package plus a deletion receipt (signed token) showing record identifiers purged and export hashes for audit. Deletion SLA for PII artifacts will be 30 calendar days after a formal purge request is accepted. We propose a MAP sub-task: "Purge validation test" performed during the residency verification milestone.

- SIG/CAIQ: we've mapped Redwood controls to the CAIQ v4 baseline; Mina attached an initial mapping workbook. If you have specific control questions, flag them per control ID to speed evidence collection.

I can pick up DPA language on the redline and propose alternative phrasing where we need to preserve platform behavior.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal Ops (contracts) — Redwood Inference

From: Remy LaFontaine <remy@finclear.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Data Protection <dataops@finclear.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 16:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Data residency & retention annex — MAP alignment for FinClear evaluation

Thanks everyone — that layout is very helpful. A couple of quick confirmations from our DPO: 

- EU residency in Ireland is acceptable. We need the purge validation test to be executed during the residency verification milestone.
- On BYOK: FinClear will opt for customer-managed keys but needs an integration checklist + estimated lead time (we will need an approximate calendar for KMS onboarding).
- Can you provide a DocuSign-ready DPA annex once you’ve accepted the redlines Karthik proposes? We’ll sign once the purge validation is completed.

Next steps:
  - Karthik, can you drop your proposed DPA language by EOD Mon (2027-06-28)?
  - Mina, can you schedule the purge validation window for 2027-07-11 to 2027-07-12?

I'll share our side of the MAP with milestone owners after we receive the DPA draft.

Remy
Product Ops — FinClear
